record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: For surface grid generation, how can a discrete variational principle be made invariant under the choice of surface parameterization, including non-smooth parameterizations, and what discrete analogue of the finite-element patch test should replace the usual finite-element patch-test condition for spatial mappings?

artifact.category_tag: discrete variational principles for surface grids
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a (possibly non-smooth) surface admitting parameterizations $\mathbf{r}: \Omega 	o S$, where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a parameter domain. A surface-grid generation method assigns to such a parameterization a discrete grid on $S$ obtained as the minimizer of some discrete functional $F_h(\mathbf{x}_1,\dots,\mathbf{x}_N; \mathbf{r})$ defined on the nodal positions of a triangulation (or quadrangulation) of $\Omega$ pulled back to $S$.

Formulate a discrete variational principle for surface grid generation with the following two properties:

(a) Parameterization invariance. For any two parameterizations $\mathbf{r}_1: \Omega_1 	o S$ and $\mathbf{r}_2: \Omega_2 	o S$ of the same surface $S$, related by a (possibly non-smooth, e.g. only Lipschitz or piecewise smooth) change of coordinates $\varphi: \Omega_1 	o \Omega_2$ with $\mathbf{r}_1 = \mathbf{r}_2 \circ \varphi$, the set of optimal grids on $S$ produced by minimizing $F_h$ is the same; equivalently, $F_h$ depends only on the intrinsic geometric data on $S$ and not on the choice of $\mathbf{r}$.

(b) Discrete patch test. State and justify a discrete analogue of the finite-element patch test, suitable for grids viewed as discrete spatial mappings $\mathbf{x}_h: \Omega 	o S$, which replaces the standard finite-element patch-test condition (exact reproduction of affine functions on a patch of elements) by an appropriate condition for the discrete grid mapping. The condition should guarantee consistency of the discrete variational principle with its continuous counterpart in the limit of mesh refinement, in a manner compatible with property (a).

Provide an explicit construction of such a functional $F_h$, prove that it satisfies (a) under the stated class of parameterization changes, and formulate and verify the corresponding discrete patch-test condition in (b).
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this problem could be located. It is posed as an open problem in a survey on variational grid generation, and there is no clear evidence in the literature of a discrete variational principle for surface grids that is provably invariant under non-smooth parameterizations together with a fully formulated discrete-mapping analogue of the finite-element patch test.
